description: Internal HTTP client for a user-profile service. In scope, Full config, Standard mode. The response is graded by RUNNING the integration test it emits across an env matrix: the gates must refuse BEFORE any network call, so none of the graded cases needs a server or a bindable socket.
_env_matrix:
Each case sets these vars and requires that outcome from `go test -tags=integration`.
  skip         = rc 0 with a --- SKIP marker (the run was not requested).
  refused      = the run FAILED *and never attempted a network call*. `fail` alone is
                 not enough: a response that ignores the prod host dials it and fails
                 on DNS, which would score as a correct refusal while doing the exact
                 dangerous thing. The gates must stop it BEFORE the call.
  reached_call = a network attempt IS visible — the gates let a legitimate config
                 through. Without this row a test that t.Fatalf's unconditionally
                 satisfies every refusal and scores perfectly.

env_matrix.name: gate unset is opt-out, not a failure
env_matrix.why: the user did not request the run — §Skip vs Fail row 1

env_matrix.name: gate on with a required var missing must be refused, never skipped
env_matrix.why: ENV is absent. A t.Skip here false-greens CI — §Skip vs Fail row 2. The removed variable must be one EVERY test in the response needs: drop one that only the first test reads and a second test legitimately proceeds and dials, which reads as 'the gate let it through'.

env_matrix.name: ENV=production must be refused
env_matrix.why: the label path; the host here is harmless loopback, so only the ENV check can stop it

env_matrix.name: bare host with no scheme must be refused (fail closed)
env_matrix.why: url.Parse accepts relative refs with no error — checking only err is a bypass. A bare host cannot be dialled either way, so this case is offline by construction

env_matrix.name: host not on NONPROD_HOST_ALLOWLIST must be refused
env_matrix.why: the allowlist is the preferred mechanism and it is fail-closed: a host that is not on it is production as far as this run is concerned. This is the case that separates a real host check from an ENV-only one, and it stays on loopback so a response that ignores it fails with a local 'connection refused'

env_matrix.name: no TEST_TENANT_ALLOWLIST must be refused (allowlist, not denylist)
env_matrix.why: a denylist is fail-open — a real prod tenant named acme-main slips through

env_matrix.name: tenant not on the allowlist must be refused
env_matrix.why: the tenant is plausible-looking and must still be refused

env_matrix.name: a fully valid non-prod config reaches the real call
env_matrix.why: the clean arm: the gates must not refuse a legitimate target. Port 1 is closed, so the run fails on a local connection refusal — which proves the call happened

_gate_markers: Substrings that identify a GATE refusal as opposed to a real call failure. Used by the `reached_call` case: if any appears, the response refused a legitimate config.
_offline: Every host in this matrix is loopback or a bare (undiallable) name. That is deliberate and load-bearing: a response that FAILS to refuse will attempt the call, so the matrix must be unable to reach anything real even when the thing under test is wrong — and the resulting error must be a local, predictable 'connection refused' rather than a DNS or sandbox message whose wording varies by environment.
_network_markers: Substrings that prove the process tried to reach the network. Presence/absence is what separates `refused` from `reached_call`.
